lifestyle-health.title: People With Type 2 Diabetes Face Up to 25 Times Higher Risk of Severe Dengue, Review Warns
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A comprehensive review highlights that diabetic patients who contract dengue for the first time face dramatically worse outcomes, a finding with urgent relevance as India enters peak monsoon season.

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India has the world's second-largest diabetes population and sees hundreds of thousands of dengue cases annually, making this finding critical for NRIs visiting family during monsoon season.

lifestyle-health.title: A 10-Minute Walk After Meals Can Slash Blood Sugar Spikes, and Experts Say Indians Need It Most
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Multiple studies show a short post-meal walk lowers glucose levels more effectively than a single long workout, a habit that could help the millions of Indians at risk of Type 2 diabetes.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person walks along a path after a meal. Research shows that even a leisurely 10-minute stroll within 30 minutes of eating can significantly reduce post-meal blood sugar spikes.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indians are genetically predisposed to Type 2 diabetes and develop it a decade earlier, making post-meal walking habits especially relevant.

lifestyle-health.image_caption: A woman works on her laptop late at night. New research links being a night owl to higher body fat, elevated blood sugar, and poorer metabolic health markers.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The findings are relevant for the Indian diaspora, where long working hours and late-night eating patterns are common, and where diabetes and metabolic syndrome rates are already elevated.

lifestyle-health.title: Fatty Pancreas Now Recognised as a Disease, Linked to Diabetes and Cancer Risk
lifestyle-health.excerpt: An international panel of experts has formally classified fatty pancreas as a distinct disease entity, establishing a clinical framework that connects pancreatic fat accumulation to type 2 diabetes and pancreatic cancer.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An anatomical illustration of the human pancreas and surrounding organs. International experts have formally classified fat accumulation in the pancreas as a distinct disease linked to diabetes and cancer.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The classification has significant implications for Indians, who face among the world's highest rates of type 2 diabetes and are increasingly affected by metabolic syndrome at younger ages.

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Pancreatic cancer disproportionately affects South Asians; AI-driven early detection breakthroughs at institutions like Johns Hopkins could improve outcomes for the Indian diaspora.

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Evening TV watching is deeply embedded in Indian family routines; findings suggest simple lifestyle adjustments could protect brain health.
